summary.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 59.37% YoY to INR3,677.03 crores, with NIM at 9.52% and gross Stage 3 at 4.65%.
summary.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q2 FY27 earnings, with disbursements up 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crores and AUM up 16.96% YoY to INR3,29,021.72 crores. Net interest income rose to INR8,661.04 crores and NIM expanded to 9.52%, which management attributed partly to temporary capital-driven benefits. Asset quality weakened, with gross Stage 3 at 4.65% (4.64% in Q1) and credit cost at 2.03%, which management linked to weak monsoon and drought-prone geographies. Management trimmed AUM growth guidance to 15-17% from 18%, and said credit cost would be elevated by about 30-40 bps for one or two quarters.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of liabilities on balance sheet
financial_highlights.change: down 15 bps QoQ from 8.56%; down 18 bps since March

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Disbursements rose to roughly INR10,000 crores per the analyst's figure, versus about INR6,000 crores in recent quarters, as lending expanded from the South and West to all-India. Unsecured share is 28% and secured 72%; MSME is a source of incremental Stage 2 and Stage 3 accretion.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold disbursements were INR5,443 crores in Q2 versus INR5,153 crores in Q1. AUM is about INR9,000 crores, and LTV is about 72-73%. Management attributes higher gold Stage 2/3 to the newly introduced EMI and interest-servicing products, where customers are used to bullet repayment.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Disbursements have rebounded, but Stage 2 and Stage 3 ratios rose. Management said absolute gross Stage 3 fell to INR862 crores from INR874 crores QoQ, and gross Stage 2 is INR963 crores versus INR953 crores, so the rise is a denominator effect.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Liability mix is public deposits 31%, NCDs 15.71%, ECB and bonds 16.5%, bank and institutional borrowing 21%, and securitisation 14%, out of total liabilities of INR2,36,271 crores. Management said about INR27,000 crores was raised in the quarter, and liquidity was brought down to about 3 months of future liabilities.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth for FY27 is now expected at 15-17%, down from the earlier 18% guidance; Q1 growth was about 15% and Q2 about 17%.
Credit cost guidance is about 2% long term. Management said it may run 30-40 bps higher in select geographies and products for one or two quarters, and the full-year figure would be lower than 2.3%.
NIM is expected to stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to around 9% in the medium term and about 8.5% in the long term.

Incremental cost of funds is expected to stay below 8%, potentially rising to about 8.35% if rates or capital market yields rise. Management does not expect the overall liability cost to rise from 8.4%.
Cost to income is guided to about 25% in the medium to long term, with technology spend likely to add to opex.
Gold loan target is unchanged: double the gold book in three years, from about 2.5% to about 5% of the book.

Insurance commission income of about INR350 crores in FY26 could fall by about INR100 crores if the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines are adopted, which management called immaterial to the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Liquidity has been drawn down to about 3 months of future liabilities, with cash plus investments falling from about INR38,000 crores to about INR31,000-32,000 crores. Future AUM growth will now largely need fresh borrowing rather than surplus liquidity.
Borrowing programme has resumed, with bonds and bank borrowing back to pre-March levels. Liquidity coverage ratio is 303%.
demand_pricing: Macro: Q1 FY27 GDP grew 7.8%, and the IMF raised its FY27 forecast to 7%. Retail CPI rose to 5.54% in September, and the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5% with a calibrated tightening stance.

Rural and auto demand: the Q2 passenger vehicle sales growth was 30.7%, two-wheelers 15.2%, and commercial vehicles 28.7%. The monsoon was 87% of LPA, and 51.2% of India's area was abnormally dry or worse as of September 23.
Stress is concentrated in drought-prone states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. Management said it is cautious there but sees no widespread problem.
New versus used vehicle yield differential is 200-400 bps, depending on the segment.
Management said fresh loans can be repriced, but the existing fixed-rate book cannot be repriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Stage 2 and Stage 3 increase across construction equipment, gold and MSME, and what credit cost is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonal weakness and certain geographies with lower rainfall, and said it is not widespread. Credit cost guidance stays at about 2%, with a possible 30 bps temporary increase in select areas. Loan-book Stage 3 is about 2.3%, not 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM and cost of funds evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM is elevated temporarily from capital infusion and will stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to about 9% medium term and about 8.5% long term. Incremental cost of funds is expected below 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AUM growth guidance lower, and are credit filters being tightened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided to 15-17% because of the West Asia war and weak monsoon, and said credit filters are unchanged unless the economy slows. Rural demand was strong in the last two quarters, and caution has only been applied to drought-prone areas in the last month.

qa_highlights.question: Are gold loan stress levels a sign of industry-level problems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is mainly from the new EMI and interest-servicing gold products, where customers used to bullet repayment are paying late, and it sees no industry-level challenge. The gold growth plan is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission was about INR350 crores in FY26, and the proposed guidelines could cut about INR100 crores. Management said this is not material to the balance sheet and expects IRDA to revise the rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex growth stay benign, and what is the medium-term cost-to-income target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included annual back-office bonuses, so Q2 staff costs normalised. The medium to long-term cost-to-income target is about 25%, with added technology spend as a risk.

risks_watch: Credit cost and Stage 3 could stay elevated for one or two quarters if the monsoon stays weak and in drought-prone areas such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.
MSME is growing fast into new geographies and carries a high share of Stage 2 and Stage 3 accretion. Unsecured exposure is 28% of the MSME book.
Rising policy rates and capital market yields could push incremental borrowing costs above 8%, and the NIM could compress faster than the guided glide path.
Management did not quantify the share of slippages from drought-prone areas or the share of new vehicles in AUM, and it referred these to investor relations.
A reported unauthorised loan issue in Kerala was taken offline, with status and KYC controls not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan Stage 2 and Stage 3 are rising as customers move to EMI and interest-servicing products.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the franchise and the H2 outlook, but cautious on growth and credit cost, which management attributes to the weak monsoon and West Asia war. It was evasive on several specifics, including EBLR migration, the new versus used split, the drought-area share of slippages and Kerala, which it deferred to investor relations.
key_quotes: It has been a good second quarter of the year for Shriram Finance under current circumstances.
So, we do not really see any kind of alarming situation in increase in the Stage 2 or Stage 1. And we have sufficient provisioning to manage this. And our guidance will remain at 2% credit cost.

The net interest margin is because of th e capital infusion, there is a temporary increase in the NIM. It is likely to remain at this level maybe for another one quarter or two, then slowly coming down.
Growth, we have been cautious, even though our initial guidance was 18% growth.
No, it's basically because we had introduced EMI and interest servicing gold loans.

growth.why: Management cut FY27 AUM growth guidance to 15-17% from 18%, citing caution, while Q2 AUM grew 16.96% YoY and disbursements 25.71%; no company-owned capacity additions were discussed, and growth is backed by lending demand and funding rather than specific capacity.
